name: COSME
summary: COSME was an early low-background, low-mass natural-germanium experiment at Canfranc, using the same detector to study WIMPs and solar axions.
detection_principle: The nuclear-recoil ionization spectrum constrains WIMP scattering. Primakoff conversion in the crystal lattice under the Bragg condition provides a direction-dependent test of solar axions.

key_parameters.name: Improvement
key_parameters.value: Background reduced by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the preceding run

results.summary: Low-mass WIMP exclusion results and constraints on axion–photon coupling were obtained.

science_scope: The WIMP analysis directly searches for Galactic dark matter. The solar-axion analysis tests candidate-particle interactions but cannot itself establish that those particles constitute Galactic dark matter.
